shift_notes.note: Index 1 lowers PIC-101 to correct a steady PV-above-setpoint offset, which a trim does not really remove, but it is a harmless 0.1 bar move.
The header is held at 2.0 bar on PIC-101 while the flange gasket is replaced, which is only acceptable because the reason says the leaking section was isolated in the field.
Index 9 runs at 140 m3/h, above the normal rate, before the overload trip has been checked; this is borderline but plausible because the pump ran cleanly at 140 earlier in the shift.
Indexes 0 and 2 raise the PIC-101 setpoint against a suction-limited pressure sag, which does little and can wind the loop up, but an operator who did not yet know the cause could plausibly try it.
Index 4 restarts the pump once after a trip of unknown cause, which is a judgement call that is common practice for a single attempt.
The pump restarts at reduced rate once the bearing has cooled, with no maintenance done; this is consistent with handing over an open problem under close watch.
